title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop. A Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final digit 2 for 7, and flagged their car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers stopped 21 year old Jaclynn Gonzales and her 12 year old sister on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another vehicle.

The sisters, one filing through their mother Janice Gonzales, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17 year old honor student who was forced to kneel in the road after a similar mistaken alert in April. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are now pending in state District Court.
